prompt: An antibody detects 50-kDa and 75-kDa bands. A validated biallelic deletion of the entire target coding sequence removes the 50-kDa band but leaves the 75-kDa band unchanged. Loading is comparable. Which interpretation is best supported?

choices.A: Both bands are proven target isoforms.
choices.B: The 50-kDa band has genetic specificity support; the 75-kDa band remains unassigned.
choices.C: Equal loading establishes the specificity of both bands.
choices.D: The remaining band proves that the genetic deletion failed.

prompt: Design a study to test whether kinase K catalytic activity, rather than its scaffolding role, is required for ligand-induced signaling and growth in a cancer cell line. Give discriminating outcomes and limits.
packet: M1: A pooled K knockout lowers phospho-S after ligand stimulation and slows growth. M2: Total S is unchanged. M3: One unvalidated kinase-dead construct is available; its abundance and folding have not been measured.

prompt: After stimulation, antibody IF suggests nuclear accumulation of factor F, but fractionation WB shows no nuclear increase. Propose competing explanations and choose the next experiment with distinct predictions.
packet: R1: IF used fixed cells and one antibody. R2: WB used an antibody against a different epitope. R3: Nuclear/cytosolic purity and recovery were not measured. R4: Total F is unchanged.

prompt: Assess the supplied citation and the claim 'A directly binds B in unmodified cells.' Separate citation identity from evidence supporting the claim.
packet: Frozen teaching dossier, retrieved 2026-10-03; identifiers refer only to this dossier. C1: The submitted citation is I. Vale, 'Native A-B recognition', 2024, record LS-M17. C2: The complete registry entry LS-M17 is J. Reed, 'Tagged protein association', 2022; no correction or retraction is recorded in this snapshot. E1: Tagged A and B were overexpressed and co-immunoprecipitated in three independent cultures, with input and IgG controls. E2: No endogenous co-IP or purified-protein binding experiment is supplied.

prompt: An enzyme follows v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]). Vmax is 90 nmol/min, Km is 20 micromolar, and [S] is 10 micromolar. What is the initial rate? Use nmol/min.
A compound lowers an enzyme's coupled fluorescence signal. Design a study to distinguish target inhibition, substrate competition and interference with the reporter system.
packet: D1: A single substrate concentration and a 30-minute endpoint were used. D2: Product detection uses a second enzyme and a fluorophore. D3: The compound absorbs near the excitation wavelength. Purified target and reporter enzymes are available.

prompt: A treatment doubles the labeled fraction of a nucleotide pool after a ten-minute isotope pulse. Does this establish doubled de novo synthesis? Propose the most informative next measurements.
packet: F1: A single endpoint fractional enrichment was measured. F2: Total pool sizes, precursor enrichment and extracellular uptake were not measured. F3: Cells may use both de novo synthesis and salvage.

prompt: Evaluate a claim that compound Q directly and selectively inhibits ribosomal peptide-bond formation. Also assess the source status of the supplied citation.
packet: Frozen teaching dossier, 2026-10-03. C1: P. Orr, 'Q regulates translation', 2025, local record BC-28; no DOI is supplied. C2: One catalog search found no matching title; catalog coverage is unspecified. E1: In cells, puromycin incorporation falls by 60% after Q. E2: ATP falls by 50% and viability is reduced. E3: No purified ribosome assay or selectivity panel is available. N1: Correction and retraction status have not been established.

prompt: A slow fluorescent calcium indicator reports a larger response on trial B than trial A. Acquisition and normalization are comparable. Which conclusion follows without additional calibration?

choices.A: Trial B contains exactly twice as many spikes.
choices.B: The indicator measures membrane voltage directly.
choices.C: The recorded indicator response is larger; exact spike counts and timing remain uncertain.
choices.D: Every neuron in the field fired synchronously.

prompt: Design an optogenetic test of whether projection P-to-Q is necessary during cue retrieval in a learned choice task. Address movement and sensory confounds.
packet: O1: P projects to Q and to another region. O2: Inhibitory opsin expression can be targeted to P neurons projecting to Q. O3: The proposed outcome is correct choices, but the task also requires locomotion. O4: Light delivery can be visible to the animal.

prompt: A circuit perturbation reduces open-arm time in a maze. The same animals move more slowly. Formulate competing explanations and select a discriminating follow-up.
packet: B1: Total distance and open-arm entries both fall. B2: No independent motor assay or sensory control was collected. B3: Scoring was unblinded and the perturbation order was fixed.

prompt: Assess source identity and the assertion that a projection is necessary for learning. Explain what the notice does and does not establish.
packet: Frozen teaching dossier, 2026-10-03. C1: The dossier archive certifies an article record NS-12, author R. Vale, title 'Projection P in learning', year 2023. The submitted citation matches every field. N1: A retraction notice states that animal identities could not be reconciled across acquisition files; it does not determine the truth of every biological claim. E1: The article reports lower learned performance after projection inhibition. E2: The allocation file and raw animal identities needed to verify independent groups are unavailable. The archive is authoritative only inside this teaching dossier.

prompt: A well-controlled GWAS identifies a lead noncoding SNP near gene G. Several linked variants span G and H. No functional or colocalization data are supplied. What follows?

choices.A: The locus is associated; identifying the causal variant and effector gene requires further evidence.
choices.B: G is necessarily the causal gene because it is closest.
choices.C: The lead SNP must be the only causal variant.
choices.D: Whole-genome sequencing alone proves the biological mechanism.

prompt: Design an analysis of paired tumor RNA, protein and metabolite measurements to identify a reproducible treatment-associated program. Explain the roles of integration, enrichment and external validation.
packet: M1: Thirty patients have pretreatment and post-treatment samples. M2: RNA and protein were run in different batches; most post-treatment metabolomics samples share a batch. M3: Some assays are missing. M4: A second small cohort is available but must remain untouched during development.

prompt: Two trajectory methods reverse a cellular ordering and assign different branch points to the same cross-sectional single-cell data. Decide what can be learned and select a follow-up that discriminates the explanations.
packet: T1: All cells were collected at one time. T2: Root selection was based on one marker. T3: Donor and processing batch partly align with the apparent branches. T4: Chromatin accessibility is available for a subset, without lineage tracing.

prompt: Assess the citation and the claim that a rare-variant burden establishes a causal disease pathway. Distinguish a source-identity decision from the strength of the analysis.
packet: Frozen teaching dossier, 2026-10-03. C1: Citation 'L. Chen, Genome-wide proof of pathway Z, Journal of Genomic Evidence, 2025, ID WG-44'. C2: A signed provenance record states that WG-44 was intentionally invented for a training exercise and was never a journal article. E1: Cases and controls were sequenced at different centers and have different ancestry distributions. E2: The burden test uses variants passing center-specific filters; coverage and relatedness are not reported. E3: Enrichment uses all annotated genes rather than genes that could pass the study's filters. N1: A journal correction/retraction state is not applicable to the invented record.
